_templatePurpose: QuizMaster schema-v3 example for BCATS Skill Standard 40540 (v1): repeatable hazard records plus existing photo evidence and learning-resource reflection.
_assessmentIntegrityNotes: Schema v3 uses generic repeatGroup blocks. SS 40540 starts with five hazard records and learners can add more hazards without changing QuizMaster code.
The repeatGroup feature is standard-agnostic: another standard can use the same engine for trials, stakeholders, tests, modifications, evaluations, or other repeated evidence records.

Five hazard records are provided as a simple PHS scaffold. The official assessment schedule does not specify a minimum number of hazards; learners still need to cover the relevant tasks, hazards and controls for their own project.
Project-stage photo evidence is repeatable so learners can cover all important stages of their project without a fixed photo count.
Project-stage photo notes combine PPE, other controls and safe work into one short prompt so the photo and explanation remain together on one evidence page.
Workplace before/after tidy-up photos are included in the same Photo Evidence page as project-stage evidence.
Cleaning/check records, damaged-tool reporting and project-instruction evidence remain in the written evidence section.
Teacher observation/sign-off is intentionally omitted in this version, as requested.
Written answers now use terminology-aware rubrics so a non-empty but unrelated answer will not receive full credit.
Rubrics accept several valid BCATS terms and synonyms; they do not require one exact sentence.
Photo-evidence notes can also require recognised safety terminology through field validation rules.

The Learner Self-reflection questions are based directly on the supplied BCATS Safety learning resource: hazards, identifying/controlling hazards, PPE, care for tools/PPE, worker responsibilities and safety documents.
Damaged/unsafe equipment evidence is conditional: learners answer Yes/No, and the report fields only appear when Yes is selected.

questionSet.label: SS 40540 - BCATS Safety
questionSet.title: Use safety practices for a BCATS project or related tasks

assessments.title: 1. Written Evidence
assessments.subtitle: Start with five hazards; add another hazard if your project needs more evidence

group.label: Start here
group.title: Your BCATS project
group.intro: Use the same project for all of this evidence.
group.reminder: Keep answers short and based on what you actually did.

questions.hint: Use the project name from your instructions.

group.label: Hazard {n} of {count}
group.title: Hazard record {n}
group.intro: Use one real project task and one hazard.
group.reminder: Keep the task, hazard, harm and control connected.

questions.hint: Name a real project task, for example measuring, marking out, cutting, drilling, assembly, sanding, finishing, or another task from your project.
Use a specific hazard term, for example noise, dust, flying debris, a sharp edge/blade, electricity, a trip hazard, chemicals, manual handling, or moving machinery.

group.label: Keep the workplace safe
group.title: Tidy, clean, check and report
group.intro: Record the practical safety evidence that is not shown by the hazard table.
group.reminder: If there was no damaged equipment, write N/A.

questions.text: How did you keep your work area tidy while you were working?
questions.hint: Include both what you DID and what you kept tidy/clear.

rubric.hint: Use an action such as tidy, clear, sweep, clean, put away, store, remove or dispose.
Name what you managed, such as tools, offcuts, rubbish, dust, leads, a walkway, bench, floor or work area.

questions.text: What tools, equipment or PPE did you clean or check after use?
questions.hint: A good answer names the item and the cleaning/check you completed.

rubric.hint: Use a cleaning/check action such as cleaned, checked, inspected, wiped, charged, washed or changed.
Name the tool, equipment or PPE item you cleaned/checked.

group.label: Damaged equipment
group.title: Damaged or unsafe equipment
group.intro: Only complete a report if you actually found damaged or unsafe tools or equipment.
group.reminder: If you select No, there is nothing else to write for this section.

question.text: Did you find any damaged or dangerous tools or equipment?
question.hint: Choose Yes only if you actually found something damaged or unsafe.

blocks.closedMessage: No damaged or unsafe equipment to report.

questions.text: What item was damaged or unsafe?
questions.hint: Name the tool, machine, equipment, or PPE item.
Use a specific fault term such as broken, cracked, frayed, loose, missing guard, faulty, worn, exposed, split, or torn.
Enter the date you found the problem, for example 29/09/2026.

questions.text: Who did you report it to?
questions.hint: Give the staff member name or role, for example teacher, technician, supervisor, or HOD.

group.label: Portfolio check
group.title: Project instructions
group.intro: The project instructions are part of the overall portfolio evidence.
group.reminder: Use the same project named at the start.

questions.text: What project instruction sheet or plan is included in your portfolio?

assessments._flexibleEngine: repeatGroup blocks are materialised at runtime by flexible-groups.js. Existing assessment grading/PDF/submission code then uses the generated normal question list.

assessments.title: 3. Learner Self-reflection - Learning Resource
assessments.subtitle: Five short questions based directly on the BCATS Safety learning resource

questionGroups.label: Learning resource reflection
questionGroups.title: What have you learned about BCATS safety?
questionGroups.intro: Answer these using the safety words and ideas from the BCATS Safety learning resource.
questionGroups.reminder: Keep your answers short, but use the correct BCATS safety terms.

questions.text: What is a hazard, and what are the THREE types of hazards in the BCATS learning resource?
questions.hint: Use the BCATS words: hazard, environmental, physical and behavioural.

questions.text: Before you start work, what must you do FIRST, and what order should you use to control a hazard?
questions.hint: Identify hazards first. Then eliminate/remove; if you cannot, minimise/reduce.

questions.text: What is PPE for? Give TWO examples of PPE from the learning resource and say what each protects you from.
questions.hint: Examples include safety glasses/goggles, hearing protection, respirators or dust masks, gloves, safety boots, protective clothing and hard hats.

questions.text: Give THREE actions from the learning resource that keep the workplace, tools or PPE safe during and after work.
questions.hint: Think about rubbish, clear work areas, inspecting/cleaning tools, checking PPE, storing gear, and reporting damage.

questions.text: What is ONE responsibility you have as a BCATS worker? Name ONE safety document from the learning resource and explain what it is used for.
questions.hint: Worker responsibilities include identifying/reporting hazards, protecting yourself and others, controlling hazards and following instructions. Safety documents include the hazard register, SOP, emergency response plan, maintenance checklist and incident report.

_finalChecklistBeforePublishing: Load flexible-groups.js after script.js and before photo-evidence.js.
Keep the five starting hazards as a PHS scaffold; + Add another hazard is available for projects needing more.
Keep the questionSet metadata as SS 40540 (v1), 4 credits.
Five hazard records are a local scaffold, not an official minimum.
Project-stage evidence remains repeatable so the learner can cover all important stages.
The Photo Evidence section keeps the photo and its short questions together on one page.
Teacher observation/sign-off remains outside this student-facing version for now.
The live-camera plugin photo-evidence.js v4 can be reused without code changes.
Keep the Learner Self-reflection aligned to the supplied BCATS Safety learning resource; do not replace it with unrelated general safety questions.

_markingRubricSummary.principle: Answers must use relevant BCATS safety terminology. Valid synonyms are accepted; unrelated filler text should not receive full credit.

hazardRecord.Project task: Real project task; project-specific wording accepted.
hazardRecord.Hazard: Must name a recognisable hazard such as noise, dust, electricity, sharp/moving equipment, trip/fall, chemicals, manual handling, etc.
hazardRecord.How it could cause harm: Must name a realistic harm/injury/illness such as hearing loss, cut, eye injury, breathing problem, burn, electric shock, strain, fall, etc.
hazardRecord.What did you do to manage it: Must name a specific control such as eliminate/remove, minimise/reduce, guard, extraction, clamp, PPE, warning others, tidy/clear area, training/supervision, etc.

_markingRubricSummary.photoEvidence: Safety notes must contain a recognised control/PPE/safe-work term before the evidence can be submitted.
